algorithm.name: Conservative token reuse with public-prefix adaptation
algorithm.strategy: Match the longest 4..8-token suffix against earlier nonoverlapping occurrences in the last 96 public generated token IDs. Copy up to four following IDs only while every occurrence agrees, requiring at least two proposed tokens. Keep at most 16 question-keyed pending proposals; on the next compatible public history infer the matched prefix, shrink to horizon 2 after a mismatch, and grow from 2 to 4 after a full observed acceptance.
algorithm.proposal_format: Exact observed token-ID list; abstain on missing or malformed fields, insufficient history, ambiguity or budget below two.
algorithm.state: At most 16 LRU tracks keyed by exact string questions up to 4096 characters. Valid supported nonterminal calls record a complete history up to 128 IDs, including abstention; budgets below two do not update tracks. Shortened or changed histories reset learning when observed. Unsupported questions and histories longer than 128 IDs use stateless reuse. Identical histories and budgets replay the same proposal, including cooldown abstention; changed budgets recompute without consuming another cooldown.
algorithm.budget_rule: At most min(4, remaining_tokens, maximum_draft_tokens, 32) token IDs. Strict integer budgets. A terminal budget below two returns without track lookup or snapshots; oversized histories first discard existing question memory.
algorithm.implementation_optimization: draft validates the full public history once, computes allowance once, and calls _reuse_validated on its bounded 96-ID window. The public reuse_tokens helper retains independent validation. Search, proposals and controller decisions are unchanged.

assumptions: generated_token_ids are the actual public committed target history and observed nonnegative integer IDs are valid in the frozen tokenizer vocabulary.
Exact verification rejects copied content when it differs; the policy does not supply unverified final answers.
Small exact-context repetitions may be predictive within some responses, but their actual frequency is unknown.
The executor may or may not preserve process state across one response; adaptation is useful only when calls share an instance.
Fixture seeds match the names of paired seeds only; Python's synthetic generator is not the frozen target random stream.
Synthetic tokenizers, equal format weights, chosen repetition frequency and cost scenarios do not estimate actual target behavior.
expected_failure_modes: Short, unique or low-repetition responses produce no acceleration and retain policy overhead.
An identical context can precede changed content; agreement among historical continuations does not guarantee the next continuation.
Useful repeats outside the 96-token window, contexts shorter than four or single-token matches are discarded.
Copying long repeated semantic content can waste verification work after a mismatch.
GPU numerical disagreement, stop and bonus conventions, real block and rollback costs remain unresolved.
Even two agreeing prior occurrences can be confidently wrong when the same context changes its continuation or reaches EOS; an executable counterexample is preserved in shift_results/analysis.json.
Even very high acceptance may fail to amortize block or policy-executor costs.
JSON state transport can dominate policy execution for long questions or histories; this cost is host-dependent and was measured only with stdlib JSON on the local CPU.
A same-question identical public state can be either a replay or a new response; no public request ID permits reliable distinction, so the controller remains idempotent.

Concurrent requests with the same question and compatible prefixes cannot be identified from this interface. Distinct exact question strings are isolated; incompatible prefixes reset learning. Returned IDs always come from the current history.

Internal block caps or skipped callbacks followed by bonus/ordinary tokens can make continuation matches differ from true verified acceptance. Internal accepted/proposed counters describe inferred matching evidence, not host-reported acceptance or a formal metric.
Final proposals often have no later callback. Terminal censorship selectively removes some full, rejected or EOS observations; the controller discards unresolved evidence on detectable restarts.
Adaptive cooldown can remove useful opportunities and costs more CPU than stateless reuse. Synthetic distributions and hypothetical verifier costs cannot choose the actual latency winner.

stochastic_boundary_research.result: PASS: 640 explicit per-position 64-element Exp(1) vectors; 2560 synthetic logit fixtures; 56320 perturbation pairs; 2560 selected boundary pairs; independent 60-digit Decimal verification; 23040 sampler-stage cast cases.
stochastic_boundary_research.interpretation: Shared noise does not guarantee shared logits, sampler-stage arithmetic or retained cache state. Support and log-margin conditions are sufficient only in ideal arithmetic under justified bounds. Refined possible-entrant conditions reduce conservative uncertainty, but observed pair errors do not certify future errors. Canonical replay must restore/rebuild retained state and reuse unchanged position noise.
stochastic_boundary_research.decision: Retain current adaptive observed-ID policy. Public state exposes no logits, q or replay authority, so introduce no numerical threshold or engine alteration. Trusted sampler and quality gates remain frozen.
stochastic_boundary_research.limitations: Synthetic logits/noise, deliberately noise-conditioned boundary fixtures and scalar rounding are not target distributions, GPU kernels, trusted sampler emulation, target equality, speedup or formal scores. Current-token stability does not certify subsequent cache-dependent decisions.
stochastic_boundary_research.next_experiment: GPU B0/B1 through the actual trusted public interface when available. Otherwise construct bounded two-step cache-residual propagation and compare current-only, uncertainty-triggered and full canonical replay, retaining a minimized next-step divergence witness.

cpu_cost_model_research.result: PASS: 128 measured arm/question/history rows, 4 arms, 4 question lengths, 8 history lengths, 5 batches and 120 repetitions per cell; 280 synthetic streams (140 character and 140 merged) priced under 4 heterogeneous target regimes; all token and call accounting identities passed.
cpu_cost_model_research.break_even: With the moderate block assumptions (55 us fixed, 9 us per compared token, 28 us rollback), adaptive ties starter at approximately 30.05 us ordinary target cost in character fixtures and 20.77 us in merged fixtures. These are model thresholds, not measured target latencies.
cpu_cost_model_research.decision: Retain adaptive reuse for the current hypothesis: it is below starter in every priced regime and has lower calibrated transport cost than fixed caps on the simulated call paths. Fixed4 is within 0.1% of adaptive in the expensive/long-block character regimes, so it remains the simplest fallback control. Add the terminal-budget fast path because no two-token proposal is legal when remaining_tokens or maximum_draft_tokens is below two; contract checks still pass (2134 states, 1004 nonempty proposals).
cpu_cost_model_research.limitations: Question strings, streams, tokenizer, acceptance patterns and target cost regimes are synthetic. JSON timings are local stdlib CPU measurements and exclude IPC. No GPU score, quality result or private data was accessed.
cpu_cost_model_research.next_experiment: When the trusted scorer is available, validate whether JSON transport is actually charged, then run paired abstention/fixed2/fixed4/adaptive latency with frozen seeds and public lifecycle probes. If transport dominates and target ordinary cost is below the thresholds, prefer abstention or fixed4; otherwise retain adaptive only after state persistence and effective-cap semantics are verified.
